title: Cache Coherence in Distributed Systems
description: Understand how multiple caches stay consistent when data changes across a distributed system.

data.text: Cache coherence is the problem of keeping multiple cached copies of the same data consistent across nodes, services, or data centers. When a system scales beyond a single cache instance, writes to the source data must be reflected across all caches. Otherwise, different users or services may see different versions of the same object at the same time.

Consider a system with two cache nodes in different regions. If a user updates a profile in Region A, the cache in Region A should invalidate its copy. Without additional coordination, the cache in Region B may continue serving the old profile for some time. This inconsistency is acceptable for some applications but unacceptable for others, such as financial systems or inventory management.

data.title: Strategies to Maintain Coherence:
items: Write-invalidate: On every write, broadcast invalidation messages to all cache nodes so they discard stale copies.
Write-update: On every write, push the updated value to all caches. More network traffic, but avoids re-fetching on the next read.
Leases: Attach a time-limited lease to cached entries so caches know when data must be revalidated from the source.
Quorum protocols: Require acknowledgments from a majority of cache replicas before confirming a write, trading latency for stronger consistency.

data.title: CAP Perspective
data.text: Strong cache coherence often requires synchronous coordination, which can reduce availability during network partitions. In practice, most large-scale systems favor eventual coherence with bounded staleness rather than strict global consistency.

Bus-based snooping protocols work well for small numbers of caches on a shared bus, but they do not scale to wide-area networks. Directory-based protocols track which caches hold copies of each item and selectively send invalidations or updates. For geo-distributed systems, hybrid approaches such as regional caches with asynchronous cross-region invalidation often offer the best balance between latency and coherence.

data.title: Coherence Design Exercise
data.description: Design a cache coherence approach for a global e-commerce product catalog updated from a single admin system.
steps: Identify the consistency requirements for product prices and descriptions.
Choose an invalidation or update strategy.
Describe how cross-region caches stay consistent during flash sales with frequent price changes.
data.expectedOutcome: A coherence design that addresses consistency, latency, and write frequency.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cache coherence prevents divergent cached copies across nodes
Invalidation is cheaper than full updates but may cause re-fetches
Quorum and lease approaches trade latency for stronger guarantees
Geo-distributed systems usually accept bounded staleness
data.takeaway: Cache coherence is a spectrum, not a boolean. Choose the weakest strategy that still satisfies your users and business rules.
